title: 1981 Paris–Dakar Rally
who: Won by René Metge (Range Rover) and Hubert Auriol (BMW)
summary: The 1981 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 18 stage towns and bivouacs through France, Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Senegal. Winners — Cars: René Metge (Range Rover); Bikes: Hubert Auriol (BMW).

sources.label: BMW Group Classic: the BMW R80 G/S Paris–Dakar

approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.name: Paris
stops.text: The start of the third Paris–Dakar.

stops.name: Olivet
stops.text: Bivouac at the end of stage 1, about 120 km from Paris.

stops.name: Sète
stops.text: Stage 2 runs about 625 km south to the port of Sète; then a day's transport to Algeria.

stops.name: Algiers
stops.text: Stage 3 starts in Algiers, with the first night in Africa at Moudjbara to the south.

stops.name: Bordj Omar Driss
stops.text: A 949 km stage 4 deep into the Algerian Sahara.

stops.name: Tit
stops.text: Stage 5: 605 km south to Tit in the Hoggar.

stops.name: Timiaouine
stops.text: Stage 6: 540 km to Timiaouine near the Malian border.

stops.name: Gao
stops.text: Stage 7: 740 km into Mali, then a rest day in Gao.

stops.name: Tombouctou
stops.text: Stage 8: 412 km up the Niger to Timbuktu.

stops.name: Bobo-Dioulasso
stops.text: Stage 10, the longest at about 1,080 km, into Upper Volta (today Burkina Faso).

stops.name: Korhogo
stops.text: Stage 12: 326 km across northern Côte d'Ivoire.

stops.name: Kolokani
stops.text: Stage 13 back into Mali, then a rest day.

stops.name: Nioro du Sahel
stops.text: Stage 14: 297 km to Nioro du Sahel.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The finish after a 96 km last stage. René Metge won the cars in a Range Rover despite gearbox trouble, and Hubert Auriol the bikes on a BMW R80 G/S.
